title: Local Mac Menu Bar Audio Normalizer for Video Creators
one_liner: A drag-and-drop macOS utility that instantaneously balances multi-track audio to YouTube -14 LUFS without cloud uploads.

pain_intensity.evidence: Annoying delay during final video exports, but not a catastrophic business killer for most creators.

frequency.evidence: Occurs 1-3 times a week during scheduled publication windows.

workaround_friction.evidence: Creators use manual volume keyframes or free Audacity plugins; tedious but functional.

paying_intent.evidence: Willing to pay a small one-off Gumroad fee ($29-$49), but high churn and reluctance for recurring SaaS subscriptions.

cross_source_recurrence.evidence: Found across X/Twitter and r/premiere, but mostly expressed as occasional workflow gripes.

competitive_gap.evidence: Auphonic, Descript, and Premiere Auto-Match exist; however, they require heavy uploads or complex multi-step settings.

feasibility_solo_buildability.evidence: Straightforward macOS Swift app wrapping ffmpeg / libebur128 audio loudness filter.

distribution_accessibility.evidence: YouTube creator community is large but fragmented; requires influencer word-of-mouth or short-form video marketing.

next_action: Archive and monitor. Adobe and Apple Final Cut Pro are likely to roll out native one-click AI loudness normalization in upcoming minor releases.
